1.title: Cabling and Physical Interface Issues
1.text: Welcome to Module twenty-one: Cabling and Physical Interface Issues. It covers the exam area five point zero Network Troubleshooting. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. five point two Given a scenario, troubleshoot common cabling and physical interface issues: cable issues (incorrect cable, signal degradation, improper termination, T X or R X transposed). Interface issues (increasing interface counters: C R C, runts, giants, drops. Port status: error disabled, administratively down, suspended). Hardware issues (Po E budget exceeded, incorrect standard. Transceiver mismatch and signal strength). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: five point zero Network Troubleshooting (twenty-four percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: Cable issues
1.text: Cable issues. Incorrect cable. Wrong type: single-mode versus multimode fiber mismatch, wrong Cat rating (Cat five for ten gigabits per second), S T P versus U T P in a noisy area, crossover versus straight-through. Signal degradation. Crosstalk (signal bleeds between pairs), interference (E M I from motors, lights, power cables), attenuation (signal weakens over distance: cable too long). Improper termination. Bad punch-down or crimp, wrong pinout (five sixty-eight A versus five sixty-eight B), untwisted pairs near the connector: slow or intermittent links, errors. T X or R X transposed. Fiber transmit and receive swapped: no link light; flip the fiber pair.

1.title: Cable issues, continued
1.text: Cable issues. The figure shows this: Cable faults: attenuation over distance, crosstalk between pairs and a bad termination. Exam tip: Cat five E or six copper runs are limited to one hundred meters. Link lights off on fiber equals check T X or R X and the transceiver.

1.title: Interface issues
1.text: Interface issues. C R C errors. Frames failed the cyclic redundancy check: bad cable, interference, duplex mismatch, bad N I C. Runts. Frames smaller than the minimum sixty-four bytes: collisions or a duplex mismatch. Giants. Frames larger than the maximum (over one thousand five hundred eighteen bytes unless jumbo is on): M T U mismatch or a faulty N I C. Drops. Frames discarded, often from congestion or full buffers.

1.title: Interface issues, continued
1.text: Interface issues. Error disabled. The switch shut the port down because of a violation (port security, B P D U guard, link flaps); fix the cause, then re-enable. Administratively down. Someone ran "shutdown"; run "no shutdown". Suspended. A link aggregation port that did not match the bundle (settings, L A C P). Exam tip: Rising C R C errors point to the cable or interference. "Err-disabled" means a security feature fired. "Administratively down" means someone disabled it.

1.title: Hardware issues
1.text: Hardware issues. Po E budget exceeded. The switch cannot power all devices (total wattage too high); some Po E devices lose power; move devices, use a bigger power budget or a different switch. Incorrect Po E standard. A device needs more power than the port offers (eight oh two dot three A F fifteen point four W, eight oh two dot three A T thirty W, eight oh two dot three B T sixty to ninety W). Transceiver mismatch. Different speed, wavelength, fiber type or protocol at the two ends: no link. Signal strength. Optical power too low or too high: dirty connector, bad fiber, wrong optic; check with a power meter. Exam tip: C R C errors point to the cable; err-disabled means a security feature shut the port; administratively down means someone shut it.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A switch port shows a rapidly increasing C R C error count. What is the most likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A faulty cable or electromagnetic interference. C R C errors point to physical-layer problems.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A fiber link shows no light after installation, although both transceivers are the same type. What should be checked first? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Whether the transmit and receive fibers are swapped. Transposed T X and R X fibers cause no link.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A switch port is shown as err-disabled after a security violation. What should the technician do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Fix the cause, then re-enable the port. Err-disabled ports need the cause fixed before re-enabling.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Several I P cameras lose power when a new camera is added to a Po E switch. What is the likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: The Po E power budget is exceeded. The switch's total Po E budget cannot supply all devices.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A ten gigabits per second link over Cat five cable runs at one hundred megabits per second with errors. What is the best fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Replace it with the correct higher-category cable. The cable category does not support the speed.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which port status means an administrator shut the port down? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Administratively down. The shutdown command sets administratively down.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does a C R C error indicate? Answer: A corrupted frame, usually from a physical-layer problem. Question two. What is a runt? Answer: A frame smaller than the minimum size. Question three. What is a giant? Answer: A frame larger than the maximum size.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is attenuation? Answer: Signal weakening over distance. Question five. What does "suspended" mean on a port? Answer: A bundled port that does not match the link aggregation settings. Question six. What is the maximum length of a copper Ethernet run? Answer: one hundred meters.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Cable: wrong type, crosstalk, E M I, attenuation, bad termination, T X or R X swapped, one hundred m limit. Counters: C R C (cable or interference), runts (collisions, duplex), giants (M T U), drops (congestion). Status: err-disabled (violation), administratively down (shutdown), suspended (L A C P mismatch). Hardware: Po E budget, Po E standard, transceiver mismatch, optical signal strength.
